nodes.summary: The 4-rank statement implies Rédei's formula. More precisely, assume the 4-rank statement. Then for every odd $d$ and every nonempty set $B$ of primes of $d$, neither the squarefreeness of $d$ nor a condition on $d_B$ modulo $8$ is needed.
nodes.title: Rédei's formula from the 4-rank statement

nodes.summary: Let $V$ be a finite set with bits $a_{ij},y_i,z_i\in\mathbb F_2$ satisfying reciprocity, and let $B\subseteq V$ be nonempty. Then the kernel of $(L_B\mid z_B)$ is trivial (the column $z_B$ counting only when $y(B)=0$) if and only if $g(B)=1$, where g(B)=\sum_{\rho\in B}z_\rho\,\kappa_\rho(B)\ \text{ if }y(B)=0,$$ and $\kappa_\rho(B)=\det L_B[B\setminus\rho,B\setminus\rho]$.
nodes.title: Rédei's bit as the triviality of a kernel

nodes.summary: Let $d$ be odd and $B$ a set of primes of $d$. Let $e_{d_B}\in\mathbb F_2^{T_{d_B}}$ be $1$ at the primes of $d_B$ and $0$ at $2$. Then every vector of $\mathbb F_2^{T_{d_B}}$ killed by the Rédei matrix of $d_B$ is $0$ or $e_{d_B}$ if and only if the kernel of $(L_B\mid z_B)$ is trivial for the bits $a,y,z$ of $d$.
nodes.title: The two kernel conditions agree
